title: Defining Carriers

children:
To be considered during routing and rating, all carriers must be defined 
 on the Carrier Window. The procedures on this page describe how to define 
 carrier and carrier service records. The carrier record is sometimes referred 
 to as the parent record. The carrier service record is sometimes referred 
 to as the child record.

The parent record represents the transportation company that offers 
 multiple services at different pricing scales, such as UPS or Fed Ex. 
 A child record represents each service provided by that carrier, such 
 as 2nd Day Delivery or Overnight Delivery. By creating separate records 
 for the carrier and its services, you can minimize setup time by using 
 inheritance. Inheritance allows you to default the appropriate carrier 
 values onto the service records. As soon as you provide a value in the 
 Carrier Field and access the Service Field, the system will display the 
 Inherited Checkbox on all other field in the Carrier Window. You can select 
 the checkbox when appropriate, instead of manually entering this information. 
 Of course, you need to define the parent record before you define the 
 child records.

Do I Need To Create Both 
 Parent & Child Records?

Before setting up a carrier, use the following question to determine 
 if you can benefit from inheritance: Does the carrier provide multiple 
 services that it charges different prices for?

If yes, you can minimize 
 setup time by creating a parent record and multiple child records. The parent record would identify the 
 carrier. Each child record would identify a specific service that the 
 carrier supported. This will allow you to inherit shared values, such 
 as address and carrier type. See the Defining the Parent Record section 
 for more details.

If no, 
 you should create just a parent record. If you only use one service provided by a carrier, or the carrier 
 does not offer any services, you will not need to inherit values across 
 multiple records. You will only need to create one parent record. See 
 the Defining a Child Record section for more details.

Note 
 On Using the Inherited Checkbox

If you select 
 the Inherited Checkbox (on any field), the system will default the value 
 from the parent record.
Can Be Used in Carrier Assignment
The following is discussed in this topic:

You will use the header fields to identify this 
 carrier as an LTL, truckload or parcel parent. You will provide values 
 in the Carrier Field and the Description Field. You will not 
 provide a value in the Service Field. The Service Field identifies a child 
 record.

Use the Type Field to select 
 what kind of carrier will transport this carrier's product, such as parcel 
 or LTL.

Use the Load Size Definition Field 
 to identify the type of trailer this carrier uses to transport product.

Use the SCAC Field to identify 
 the carrier's SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) value. The carrier will 
 supply this code.

Use the Shipping Calendar Field 
 to associate this carrier with the appropriate shipping calendar record. 
 These define "no ship days," such as holidays.

Use the Pro Number Set Name Field 
 to associate the carrier with its Pro Numbers. The carrier will supply 
 these numbers. This is only done if the carrier is an LTL or truckload 
 carrier.

Use the Can Be 
 Used to Ship Checkbox to indicate if this carrier can ship product. 
 Generally, you will want to select this checkbox unless you are creating 
 a parent record that is used for inheritance purposes only.

If you are defining a parent 
 record only, select this checkbox for the parent record.

If you are defining both parent 
 & child records, do not select this checkbox for the parent 
 record if its only used for inheritance purposes. Later, when you create 
 the child records, you will select this checkbox for each child record.

Use the Can Be Used in Carrier 
 Assignment Checkbox to indicate if this carrier can be rated. Carriers 
 that the system cannot select during assignment can be manually selected.

If this carrier can accommodate 
 most of your shipments, select this checkbox. During rating, the 
 system will include this carrier and might select it.

If this 
 carrier rarely transports product for you, consider not selecting 
 this checkbox. This will minimize processing time. You can still select 
 this carrier manually.

Use the Address 
 Tab fields to provide the carrier's billing address. You can also 
 identify your contact name at the carrier, his/her phone number and fax 
 number.

This tab is only required if you plan to use the rating module. Note: 
 you will not be able to complete this tab's values until you finish the 
 Rating Setup procedures.

Use the Charge 
 Requirement Buttons to indicate whether rating is 'not required', calls an associated internal or external rating engine (system calculated)or is 'manually' added to the shipment.

Use the Rating ID Field 
 to identify the server/carrier symbols used to identify where rating is coming from.  .
Use the Rating Service Field to identify a carrier/service combination. It is used by the system to call external rating engines. For LTL internal rating, this field should be left blank.

Use the Rating 
 Profile Field to associate a profile record to this carrier. When 
 rating is run during a wave, the system usually does not know how many 
 containers are on a shipment. It uses the rating profile to estimate how 
 many containers are on a shipment.
Use the FAK LTL Class Field for LTL internal rating. If you want the entire shipment to get rated at the specified LTL Class regardless of the actual classes of the items on the shipment.

Use the Commitments 
 Required for Routing Checkbox to identify how the system will make 
 a carrier decision during routing, when a particular carrier is part of 
 a carrier group. The following is based on when a carrier commitment record            does not exist for a certain 
 carrier:

If this 
 checkbox is checked, commitments are required for this carrier. 
 Therefore, the system will reject this carrier because no commitment record 
 exists.

If this 
 checkbox is not checked, that indicates that commitments are not 
 required for this carrier. Therefore, the system will not reject the carrier. 
 However, a large number of days to deliver is used (999), which makes 
 it almost impossible for that carrier to "win" the selection 
 process and be assigned to the shipment.

Use the Email Address Field 
 to provide your contact person's email address.

Use the Web Site Field to 
 provide the carrier's website address.

Use the Internet Tracking Link 
 Field to identify the carrier's tracking parcels website. This 
 value is required if you want to link a container ID to its carrier's 
 web page in Trading Partner Management. You can obtain this value from 
 the particular carrier that you are linking to.

Use the Available 
 for Web Order Checkbox to indicate that you want to be able to 
 choose this carrier when entering a web order via Trading Partner Management.
Use the Consolidation Location Area Field to indicate the default dock location area you want to use when consolidating this carrier's shipments.

After you define the parcel parent record, you can create the parent 
 child records. These records identify a specific service offered by the 
 carrier that you defined on the parcel parent record. If an LTL or truckload 
 carrier offers services, you can create child records for it.

In the Carrier Field, identify 
 the carrier that offers this service, or the parent carrier. Make sure 
 that you enter this value exactly as it appears on the parent record. 
 When you exit this field and enter the Service Field, the system will 
 recognize that you are creating a child record. It will display the Inherited 
 Checkbox on each field that can obtain its value from the parent record.

In the Service 
 Field, identify the service level that you want to define a record 
 for. The value in this field, along with the value in the Carrier Field, 
 will identify this record to the system.
